reason: SOR/2025-275 re-opened (current to 2026-09-21, last amended 2026-03-31): Schedule 3 item 7 boundary confirmed; the midpoint of the boundary turning points 44°09'30.3"N 66°47'01"W and 44°11'50.3"N 66°49'31"W is exactly 44°10'40.3"N 66°48'16"W, the position recorded for RAMN calling-in point 1A, so the zone's outer limit crosses the TSS entrance and the zone takes in all Canadian waters landward to the US boundary. Sections 26 and 27 (sailing plans, position reports at RAMN calling-in points) are the zone's own duties, so treating them as part of the VTS and not a separate MRS is right. The CCG RAMN 2026 page could not be re-opened (server reset the connection twice), so I could not check the Table 3-30 wording directly. The statutory boundary alone meets association standard item 3.

Keep 'Neither confirmed' but correct the basis. The claim that Table 1 to 33 CFR 161.12(c) 'lists every VTS' is false: Table 1 has 12 entries (Berwick Bay to St. Marys River) and omits VTS Tampa, which NAVCEN lists as an operating VTS (a Coast Guard/Tampa Port Authority cooperative service not established in Part 161). A US VTS can therefore exist outside Part 161. Also, the NAVCEN overview (Z1-S5) says '12' centres, then names 13 and leaves out Lower Mississippi River, so it is not a clean enumeration. Absence should rest on: 33 CFR 161.2 (VTS is a USCG service), 161.6 (federal preemption of state law on VTS), the NAVCEN VTS Locations page (12 VTS, including Tampa, none in Maine), and current US Coast Pilot 1 ch. 9 (27 Sep 2026 edition), which covers Portland and mentions no VTS or traffic reporting service. Together this is enough authoritative evidence of absence. WHALESNORTH exclusion re-checked: the northern edge is 42°39'N to 42°45'N and the TSS is north of 43°07'N.

Geometry re-checked against 33 CFR 169.105 and 167.76-77 (eCFR 2026-09-01). At 42°05'N the southbound outer lane edge is at about 69°55'W, east of the 70°02'W west edge. At 41°00'N the lanes run from about 69°05'W to 69°11'W, inside 68°31'W to 69°17'W. The north-eastern boundary (42°45'N 70°13'W to 42°10'N 68°31'W) is at about 42°41'N where the TSS reaches 70°01'W, well north of the TSS. So everything north of 41°00'N is inside WHALESNORTH, and the lane ends and junction precautionary area south of 41°00'N are outside. MRS only, partial, is correct. The 'no USCG VTS' finding has the same wording flaw as TSS-0197 (Table 1 is not a complete list, because Tampa is missing), but NAVCEN Locations and 161.2/161.6 still support it.

Keep 'Neither confirmed'. Fix the same false 'Table 1 lists every VTS' wording as TSS-0197 and add current US Coast Pilot 2 ch. 7 (27 Sep 2026), which covers the Narragansett/Buzzards Bay TSS and mentions no VTS. VMRS Buzzards Bay check reproduced: my calculation puts the Buzzards Bay approach end about 2.9 to 3.4 NM south of the Sakonnet Point to Buzzards Bay Entrance Light line (the record says about 3.3 to 3.8 NM). The difference is small and does not change the result that the VMRS adjoins but does not cover the TSS. The Narragansett northern precautionary area (centre 71°23.3'W, radius 3.55 NM) is west of Sakonnet Point. 33 CFR 160 notice of arrival is a port-entry notification and 165 RNAs impose situational or VMRS-repeating duties, so neither is a ship reporting scheme covering the TSS. The Block Island Sound Seasonal Management Area (50 CFR 224.105) is a speed rule, not reporting.

The 161.25 and Table 1 item (7) southern boundary (Ambrose, Swash and Sandy Hook entrance buoys to Sandy Hook Point) is confirmed. Ambrose Buoy 1 (40.46876N 73.87223W) is 1.95 NM from the precautionary circle centre (7 NM radius), so the VTS boundary does cross the circle. My Monte Carlo estimate, with approximate Breezy Point, Swash and Sandy Hook buoy positions, is 6 to 7% of the circle inside the VTS area. The record's 'about 8%' is the right order but should read 'roughly 5 to 10%'. Lanes and separation zones end at 073°40'W to 073°49'W south and east of the boundary, so they are outside. The currency flag on the proposed discontinuance of the Ambrose buoys is appropriate and should stay.

Keep 'Neither confirmed' for VTS and MRS, but the record misses the key official source and cites an encyclopedia (lead-only). US Coast Pilot 3 ch. 6 (27 Sep 2026 edition) states that 'Vessels arriving at the Delaware Bay entrance are advised to contact the voluntary vessel traffic information service through the Delaware Pilot traffic tower on VHF-FM channel 14. Contact should be made upon a vessel's entrance into the appropriate sea-lane'. It also says a Maritime Exchange/Pilots communication system ('Cape Henlopen Tower') provides ship reporting services, with reporting only 'recommended'. This is a voluntary, private (pilots' association) service, not a VTS implemented by the competent authority (33 CFR 161.2; state VTS law is pre-empted by 161.6), and it is not mandatory. So: set voluntary_reporting to 'Yes' (Delaware Pilots VTIS and Maritime Exchange, Ch 14, contact on entering the sea-lanes), record the pilots' VTIS in vts_leads, replace Z1-S19 with Coast Pilot 3 ch. 6, and fix the 'Table 1 lists every VTS' wording as in TSS-0197. If the coordinator's VTS definition takes in non-government traffic information services, this becomes 'Unresolved', not VTS only.

Keep 'Neither confirmed'. Fix the false 'Table 1 lists every VTS' wording (VTS Tampa is missing from Table 1) and add current US Coast Pilot 3 ch. 9 (27 Sep 2026), which describes the Chesapeake Bay TSS and mentions no VTS or traffic information service. 33 CFR 165.501 re-checked: the RNA Offshore Zone reaches the territorial sea boundary and so contains the TSS, but its duties are situational (impaired manoeuvrability, emergencies near the bridge-tunnels, equipment carriage), not a ship reporting scheme. Treating it as not an MRS is right, but it is worth noting in the record that the RNA covers the TSS.

Keep 'Neither confirmed'. Fix the 'Table 1 lists every VTS' wording as in TSS-0197 and add current US Coast Pilot 4 ch. 5 and ch. 6 (27 Sep 2026), which cover the Cape Fear River approaches with no VTS or traffic reporting service mentioned. NAVCEN Locations lists no Wilmington or Cape Fear VTS. The TSS (about 33°32'N to 33°50'N) is outside both WHALES areas (WHALESSOUTH limit 31°27'N).

161.35(a) (Galveston Bay Entrance and Outer Bar Channels) and the Table 1 item (3) box confirmed. My distances from the Galveston south jetty tip: inshore precautionary area 2.6 to 6.1 NM, landward lane ends about 5.5 to 6 NM, seaward lane ends about 17 NM, offshore precautionary area 17 to 21 NM. This matches the record's partial split at the 12 NM territorial sea. NAVCEN's 'from the sea buoy' wording might put the operational area further out, but it would not change 'VTS only, partial'.

The ASIPONA 'Área de influencia' page re-opened (2026 footer) confirms 'El área de control de tráfico marítimo ejercido por el CCTMVER, incluye las zonas de separación de tráfico, carriles, áreas de precaución, área a evitar y área de fondeo' and the five boundary points. It does not use 'VTS'. Accepting this as a VTS link is reasonable: an official port traffic control centre whose defined area expressly names the TSS meets association standard items 1 and 3. In Mexican practice the CCTM is the centre from which the 'Servicio de Tráfico Marítimo' is provided under the Ley de Navegación y Comercio Marítimos and IMO A.857(20), as the API Altamira CCTM operating rules show (a different port and dated 2009, so supporting context only). Keep the unresolved note asking for SEMAR or ALRS Vol 6 confirmation of designation and mandatory participation, and keep coverage as partial.
